---
title: "Tournament Game Generator"
resources:
  - generate_games_from_event_link.py
  - eventLinkPlugin.zip 
---

Use this page to generate formatted match results directly in your browser.
Everything runs locally — no upload to any server.

```{=html}
<div id="py-tool" class="card p-3 mt-3">
  <h4>Generate games from CSVs</h4>

  <div class="mb-3">
    <label for="correspondenceFile" class="form-label">Player–Deck mapping (CSV)</label>
    <input type="file" id="correspondenceFile" class="form-control">
  </div>

  <div class="mb-3">
    <label for="resultsFile" class="form-label">Results file (CSV)</label>
    <input type="file" id="resultsFile" class="form-control">
  </div>

  <button id="runButton" class="btn btn-primary">Run generator</button>
  <button id="downloadButton" class="btn btn-success ms-2" style="display:none;">📥 Download results</button>

  <div class="mt-3">
    <label for="output" class="form-label">Errors / Logs</label>
    <textarea id="output" class="form-control" rows="10"
      placeholder="Any errors will appear here..." readonly></textarea>
  </div>
</div>

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.26.2/full/pyodide.js"></script>
<script>
async function main() {
  const pyodide = await loadPyodide();
  await pyodide.loadPackage("pandas");

  const runButton = document.getElementById("runButton");
  const downloadButton = document.getElementById("downloadButton");
  const outBox = document.getElementById("output");

  runButton.onclick = async () => {
    const corr = document.getElementById("correspondenceFile").files[0];
    const res = document.getElementById("resultsFile").files[0];
    if (!corr || !res) {
      alert("Please upload both CSV files");
      return;
    }

    // Reset state
    outBox.value = "";
    downloadButton.style.display = "none";

    const pyCode = await fetch("generate_games_from_event_link.py").then(r => r.text());
    pyodide.FS.writeFile("corr.csv", await corr.text());
    pyodide.FS.writeFile("res.csv", await res.text());

    // Capture stdout/stderr
    let stdout = "";
    let stderr = "";
    pyodide.setStdout({ batched: (s) => { stdout += s; } });
    pyodide.setStderr({ batched: (s) => { stderr += s; } });

    const wrapped = `
import sys, io, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)
sys.argv = ['script','corr.csv','res.csv']
${pyCode}
    `;

    outBox.value = "⏳ Running...";
    try {
      await pyodide.runPythonAsync(wrapped);

    if (stderr.trim()) {
        const normalized = stderr.replace(/\r?\n/g, "\r\n");
        outBox.value = "❌ Error(s):\n" + normalized;
      } 
      // No error → enable download
      const normalized = stdout.replace(/\r?\n/g, "\r\n");
      const blob = new Blob([normalized], { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8" });
      const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
      downloadButton.onclick = () => {
        const a = document.createElement("a");
        a.href = url;
        a.download = "generated_results.csv";
        a.click();
        URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
      };
      downloadButton.style.display = "inline-block";
      outBox.value = "✅ Generation successful! Click 'Download results' to save the CSV.";
      
    } catch (err) {
      const normalized = stderr.replace(/\r?\n/g, "\r\n");
      outBox.value = "❌ Error(s):\n" + normalized;;
      console.error(err);
    }
  };
}
main();
</script>
```

---

### Inputs

- **Player-Deck mapping** is expecting a **[CSV file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comma-separated_values)**, using
',' (comma) as separator, corresponding to the header "Player","Deck".

> 🧰 Coming soon: some way to generate such file from a table Player <-> DeckURL


- Results file must be a CSV file too, also using ',' (comma) as separator, corresponding to the header
  Table,"Player 1","Player 2","MatchResult". This one can be generated easily from eventlink using a small chrome
  plugin (see **Chrome Plugin** below).

### Chrome Plugin

  A Google Chrome plugin is a simple small code that runs locally within your browser. In this case, it simply look at
  the current web page, and tries to read the values for the players, tables and game results.

  To use the plugin, start by downloading **[this zip file](eventLinkPlugin.zip)** containing everything required.
  Unzip it somewhere you can find it, then open Google Chrome. Go into  "Extension" > "Manage extensions". Be sure
  to check the "Developer mode" at the top right corner. Then click "Load unpacked" and select the directory you just
  downloaded (eventLinkPlugin).

  Congrats! You just installed the plugin. Now if you click on the extensions symbol again, you should see it.
  For convenience, you can also pin it, so it keeps appearing at the top of your browser. Open an eventlink page,
  and select a round that has finished. Click on the "extract results", and that's it. You can now paste the result
  in a CSV file. Be carefull if you provide multiple rounds at once, the header (the line "Table,Player 1,Player 2,
  MatchResult") will show multiple times. Simply remove each occurence, except for the first one.
